function_v0.doc:
Set the admin, the asset names are paid in, and where payments go.

`pay_token` is a SAC address \xe2\x80\x94 USDC's \xe2\x80\x94 and `treasury` the account that
receives it.
function_v0.name: initialize

function_v0.doc:
Who currently holds the admin role.

Worth exposing because the admin can replace this contract's logic, so
"who is it" is a thing a holder is entitled to check rather than infer
from deployment notes.
function_v0.name: get_admin

function_v0.doc:
Replace this contract's WASM.

The registry holds names people paid for, so it cannot be replaced by
deploying a second one \xe2\x80\x94 a new contract starts empty and every existing
name stays in the old one. An upgrade is the only way to correct a
price band, the recovery window or a term bound after launch.

`new_wasm_hash` must already be uploaded to the ledger. Nothing here
checks that the incoming WASM keeps this contract's storage layout; a
mismatched upgrade reads existing `Record` entries as garbage, so the
replacement has to be built from this source, not merely resemble it.
function_v0.name: upgrade

function_v0.doc:
Hand the admin role to someone else.

The point of this is to get the admin out of a single key: a multisig
or a timelock contract is a valid `new_admin`. There is deliberately no
way to renounce the role by setting it to a burn address \xe2\x80\x94 that would
freeze the reserved-name list and the upgrade path together, which is
the state this contract was changed to avoid.
function_v0.name: set_admin

function_v0.doc:
Mark names nobody may register.

Admin-held rather than compiled in because the list will certainly need
adding to \xe2\x80\x94 a partner brand, a product name that does not exist yet.
Keeping it in storage means adding one is an admin call rather than an
upgrade.
function_v0.name: reserve

function_v0.doc: What a registration would cost, in stroops of the payment asset.
function_v0.name: quote

function_v0.doc:
Where a name points, or `None` if it does not resolve.

This is what federation answers from. An expired name returns `None`
from the instant it lapses \xe2\x80\x94 no grace. A name that still resolves after
its term is a name whose holder believes it is working.
function_v0.name: resolve

function_v0.doc: When a name runs out, whether or not it already has.
function_v0.name: expires_at

function_v0.doc: Active, in recovery, or open to anyone.
function_v0.name: state

function_v0.doc:
Register a name and take payment for it in one invocation.

Payment and issuance are deliberately the same call: split across two,
a transfer that lands while the mint fails leaves somebody out of
pocket with nothing to show, which is the failure the offramp already
needs a whole table to track. Here it cannot happen \xe2\x80\x94 either both
happen or the transaction reverts.

Returns the new token id.
function_v0.name: register

function_v0.doc:
Extend a name's term. Anyone may pay.

There is no access check here and that is deliberate. Renewal only ever
extends a name for its current holder \xe2\x80\x94 it cannot move it, re-point it
or take it \xe2\x80\x94 so the worst a stranger can do is pay somebody's bill.
Refusing that would mean a name lapsing because its holder lost their
phone in the wrong week while a friend would gladly have covered it.
function_v0.name: renew

function_v0.doc: Point a name at a different address without moving the token.\n\nOnly the holder, and only while the name is active.
function_v0.name: set_target
